<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Autocancel background agent</issue_title>
> <issue_description> Conceptual Definition
> Purpose:
> AI-driven background agent that evaluates Assigned work orders and auto-cancels those meeting defined criteria.
> 
> Triggers:
> Polling loop every 5 seconds while UI.Server is running.
> 
> Decision Criteria:
> 
> Work order assigned more than 24 hours ago
> Description contains “test”, “demo”, or “temporary” (case-insensitive)
> Room number equals or resembles “TEST”
> Outcomes:
> If criteria are met, transitions status from Assigned → Cancelled via domain command using the creator as the acting user.
> 
> 🎨 User Experience Design
> Interface:
> No direct UI; runs transparently on the server.
> 
> Visible Effects:
> 
> Work Order Search Grid: Items may flip from Assigned to Cancelled without manual action
> Work Order Details Page: Status reflects Cancelled after processing
> Audit Consistency: Cancellation attributed to the work order’s creator
> Timing Expectation:
> Evaluation takes effect within ~5 seconds after assignment or data change.
> 
> ⚙️ Technical Design
> Hosting
> AutoCancelAgentService registered as a BackgroundService in UI.Server; starts with the app
> Loop implemented via ExecuteAsync with cancellation token
> 5-second delay using TimeProvider; includes error handling with back-off
> Data Access & Actions
> Uses IBus.Send for:
> WorkOrderSpecificationQuery with MatchStatus(WorkOrderStatus.Assigned)
> EmployeeByUserNameQuery to hydrate workOrder.Creator
> AssignedToCancelledCommand to perform status transition
> AI Agent
> Decision logic encapsulated in WorkOrderEvaluationAgent.ShouldCancelWorkOrderAsync
> Agent prompt:
> “You are an AI agent responsible for evaluating work orders for automatic cancellation…”
> 
> Interfaces:
> Uses Microsoft.Extensions.AI agent interfaces and ChatClientFactory
> Scoping & Resilience
> IServiceScope created once for evaluation; separate scope for command execution
> Logs:
> At start/stop
> Per-iteration errors
> Per-work-order exceptions (loop continues)
> Skips cancellation if Creator is null; logs warning
> Constraints
> Only processes work orders with Assigned status
> Assumes idempotency by domain command handlers
> Stack: .NET 9, C# 13, Blazor WASM hosted backend in UI.Server
> ✅ Test Scenarios to Develop
> Acceptance/UI (Playwright)
> Work order with description “test demo temporary” → Cancelled within 6–10 seconds
> Room number “TEST” → Cancelled within 6–10 seconds
> Assigned > 24 hours ago → Cancelled
> Recent Assigned → Remains Assigned
> No matching criteria → Remains Assigned after 10+ seconds
> Integration
> WorkOrderSpecificationQuery.MatchStatus(Assigned) returns only Assigned items
> EmployeeByUserNameQuery hydrates creator; null creator → no cancellation + warning log
> AssignedToCancelledCommand transitions status and records actor as creator
> Agent Logic
> ShouldCancelWorkOrderAsync returns true for:
> 
> Description with “test”, “demo”, “temporary” (varied cases/punctuation)
> Room number variants: “TEST”, “Test”, “test-001”
> AssignedDate older than 24 hours (boundary: 24h + 1s)
> Returns false for:
> 
> Near-threshold (e.g., 23h59m)
> Non-matching text
> Reliability
> Handles transient IBus errors; continues processing
> Prevents double-cancel if item already Cancelled
> Honors cancellation token on shutdown (no blocking)
> </issue_description>

body:
# Fix lint command to accept direct files without extension filter

## Summary

Fixed an issue where the `lint` command required the `--extension` flag even when users explicitly provided direct file paths with custom extensions (e.g., `.json.schema`). 

**Key changes:**
- Modified `handle_json_entry()` in `src/utils.cc` to skip extension filtering for direct file paths
- Extension filtering is preserved for directory traversal (where it makes sense to filter by type)
- Added test case covering files with custom extensions like `.json.schema`

The fix distinguishes between two use cases:
1. **Directory traversal**: Still filters by extension (`.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml` by default)
2. **Direct file paths**: No extension filtering - if user explicitly provides a file path, process it regardless of extension

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify requirement understanding**: Test that files with custom extensions (like `.json.schema`) can now be processed without `--extension` flag
- [ ] **Test edge cases**: Try passing non-schema files (text files, binaries, files without extensions) to ensure graceful handling
- [ ] **Confirm directory behavior unchanged**: Verify that directory scanning still respects extension filtering and doesn't process unexpected file types
- [ ] **Test mixed scenarios**: Try commands that combine direct file paths and directory arguments to ensure both behaviors work correctly

### Recommended Test Plan
```bash
# Should work without --extension (new behavior)
./jsonschema lint my-schema.json.schema

# Should still work with directories (unchanged behavior)  
./jsonschema lint ./schemas/

# Should still respect --extension for directories
./jsonschema lint --extension .custom ./schemas/
```

### Notes

**Potential risks to consider:**
- This removes a safety mechanism that prevented processing of non-schema files when explicitly provided
- The behavior change is intentional but could surprise users who relied on extension filtering as validation

body:
## Overview

This PR implements a complete monitoring and alerting system for the arbitrage bot, addressing the critical need for operational awareness, early issue detection, and performance optimization. The system provides real-time metrics tracking, multi-channel alerting, automated incident response, and comprehensive health monitoring.

## 🏗️ Architecture

The monitoring system consists of 8 core services orchestrated by a central integration layer:

```
CoreArbitrageEngine ←→ MonitoringIntegration ←→ DashboardAPI
                              ↓
        ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐
        │                     │                     │
   AlertManager        HealthMonitor      PerformanceAnalyzer
        │                     │                     │
   LogAnalyzer      InfrastructureMonitor    IncidentManager
        │                     │                     │
        └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘
                              │
                      MetricsDashboard
```

## 🚀 Key Features

### Real-time Performance Monitoring
- **Trading Metrics**: Profit/loss tracking, win rates, execution times, success rates
- **System Metrics**: CPU usage, memory consumption, network latency monitoring
- **Market Metrics**: Opportunity detection rates, market condition indicators
- **Risk Metrics**: Current exposure, risk score distribution, slippage analysis

### Multi-Channel Alerting System
- **Discord Integration**: Rich embeds with color-coded priorities and webhook support
- **Telegram Bot**: Interactive commands, status queries, and real-time notifications
- **Email Notifications**: Detailed reports with SMTP support and attachments
- **Slack Integration**: Channel-specific routing with mentions and threading
- **SMS Alerts**: Critical emergency notifications via Twilio integration
- **Push Notifications**: Browser and mobile app notifications with VAPID support

### Intelligent Monitoring
- **Anomaly Detection**: Statistical analysis (3σ threshold) for unusual patterns
- **Bottleneck Identification**: Automated performance issue detection and recommendations
- **Health Scoring**: Component-level and overall system health with trend analysis
- **Predictive Alerts**: Early warning system based on historical patterns

### Automated Response
- **Self-Healing**: Automatic recovery procedures for common system issues
- **Failover Management**: Seamless switching to backup RPC providers and services
- **Incident Escalation**: Progressive alert severity with configurable thresholds
- **Recovery Validation**: Automated verification of fixes and system restoration

## 📊 Implementation Details

### Core Services Added

1. **`MonitoringIntegration.js`** - Central orchestration service that connects all monitoring components with the CoreArbitrageEngine through event-driven integration
2. **`MetricsDashboard.js`** - Real-time dashboard with WebSocket support for live updates, interactive charts, and system topology visualization
3. **`AlertManager.js`** - Enhanced multi-channel alert system with smart throttling, rate limiting, and priority-based routing
4. **`HealthMonitor.js`** - Comprehensive health monitoring with automated recovery, dependency tracking, and performance benchmarking
5. **`PerformanceAnalyzer.js`** - Advanced analytics with bottleneck detection, SLA compliance monitoring, and optimization recommendations
6. **`LogAnalyzer.js`** - Centralized logging with pattern recognition, anomaly detection, and real-time streaming capabilities
7. **`InfrastructureMonitor.js`** - Network and RPC provider monitoring with auto-optimization and bandwidth tracking
8. **`IncidentManager.js`** - Automated incident detection and response with escalation procedures and recovery validation
9. **`DashboardAPI.js`** - RESTful API with authentication, rate limiting, and mobile-responsive endpoints

### Configuration System

- **`src/config/monitoring.js`** - Comprehensive configuration system with environment variable support
- **`.env.monitoring.example`** - Complete template with all available configuration options
- Environment-based overrides for development, testing, and production deployments

### Integration with Existing System

The monitoring system integrates seamlessly with the existing `CoreArbitrageEngine` through:

- **Event-driven Architecture**: Listens to existing engine events without modifying core logic
- **Method Injection**: Adds performance measurement hooks to critical methods

author: zonotope
body:
This patch primarily ensures that the ledger alias for new commits includes the branch name. If the previous commit's ledger alias did not include a branch name, then "main" is assumed and appended to the existing alias. The branch name is also ensured in the ledger alias stored in a connection's ledger cache.

This patch also modifies the `fluree.db.util.ledger/ensure-ledger-branch` function was modified so that when `""` or `nil` was passed in as a ledger name, no branch would be appended.

The `fluree.db.nameservice.sub` namespace was removed with it's functionality consolidated with the `fluree.db.connection` namespace. First, there were duplicate `notify` functions both in the `fluree.db.connection` and `fluree.db.nameservice.sub` namespaces, but different code paths used each one. This would have led to bugs as each function was modified and diverged. Next, all of the functions in this namespace operated on connection records, so they should be in the connection hierarchy. If the connection namespace is too big, then we should refactor connections into discrete components with limited functionality, and pass those components to other namespaces if necessary (like a `subscriber` component within a connection, for example). 

Lastly, I removed some unused functions.

body:
### 작업 요약
- **FCM HTTP v1**로 PWA 학생들에게 공지 알림 발송 기능 구현.
- 구독(토큰) 관리, 수동/자동(웹훅) 발송, 무효 토큰 자동 비활성화, 발송 결과 로깅 제공.

### 주요 변경 사항
- **알림 클라이언트**
  - `src/utils/fcm_client.py`: OAuth2 토큰 발급, 단건/멀티 발송, 무효 토큰 판정 로직.
- **서비스**
  - `src/services/subscriptions_service.py`: 구독 생성/업데이트(UPSERT), 상태 조회, 무효 토큰 비활성화.
  - `src/services/notifications_service.py`: 활성 구독 조회, 전송 오케스트레이션, `notify.notice_logs` 로깅.
- **핸들러**
  - `src/handlers/subscriptions_handler.py`: `POST /subscriptions`, `GET /subscriptions/status`.
  - `src/handlers/notifications_handler.py`: `POST /notifications`, `POST /webhook/notify`, `POST /webhook/test`.
- **DTO**
  - `src/dto/notification_dto.py`: `SubscriptionDTO`, `SubscriptionCreateRequestDTO`, `NotificationLogDTO` (+ `@dataclass`).
  - `src/dto/__init__.py`: 신규 DTO export 추가.
- **문서/배포**
  - `docs/openapi.yml`: 스키마와 경로 추가(Subscriptions/Notifications/Webhook).
  - `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: Secrets(Base64) → `envs/firebase-service-account.json` 생성, 환경 파일 생성, 서버리스 배포.
  - `serverless.yml`: `envs/firebase-service-account.json`만 패키징에 포함, 환경변수 주입.

### 신규/변경 API
- `POST /subscriptions`
  - Body: `{ fcm_token, student_no, platform }`
  - 동작: 토큰 기준 UPSERT로 활성화/갱신
- `GET /subscriptions/status?fcm_token=...`
  - 동작: 구독 상태 조회
- `POST /notifications`
  - Body: `{ title, body, notice_id, data? }`
  - 동작: 활성 구독 전체 대상 수동 발송 + 결과 로깅
- `POST /webhook/notify`
  - Header: `x-webhook-secret: ${WEBHOOK_SECRET}`
  - Body: Supabase DB Webhook Payload
  - 동작: `core.notice` INSERT 이벤트 → 자동 발송

### 환경 변수 추가
- `FCM_PROJECT_ID`
- `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH` = `envs/firebase-service-account.json`
- `WEBHOOK_SECRET`
- `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` 파일

### CI/CD (GitHub Actions)
- `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` 시크릿을 디코드해 `envs/firebase-service-account.json` 생성.
- `envs/config.dev.json`/`envs/config.prod.json` 생성 시 `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH`를 동일 경로로 설정.
- `serverless.yml`에서 `envs/firebase-service-account.json`만 패키징 포함.

### 데이터 처리/로깅
- 전송 결과를 `notify.notice_logs`에 기록.
- FCM 응답의 코드/메시지 기반으로 무효 토큰 판정 → `notify.subscriptions.is_active=false` 자동 비활성화.

### 테스트 가이드

**토큰 등록**
   - 프론트(PWA)에서 FCM 토큰 발급 후 `POST /subscriptions` 호출.

**자동 발송 확인**
   - Supabase에서 `core.notice`에 INSERT → 웹훅 → 알림 수신 및 `notify.notice_logs` 기록 확인.

- [ ] ❓ Other (about what?)

### 🔗 Related Issues

### 💡 Background and Solution

The Pagination component  currently supports the `itemActiveBg` prop to customize the background color of the active item. However, it does not support modifying the text color of the active item. This results in poor contrast between the text (which uses the primary color) and the background when a dark `itemActiveBg` is set, making the text unreadable.

Add two new props, `itemActiveColor` and `itemActiveColorHover`, to the Pagination component. These props will allow customization of the text color of the active item (for the default state and hover state respectively), resolving the low-contrast issue and enabling full visual customization of active pagination items.

### 📝 Change Log

> - Describe the impact of the changes on developers, not the solution approach.

author: unclesp1d3r
body:
Summary
- Adds numeric section weighting to prioritize likely string-bearing areas and refines ELF import discovery to make symbol extraction more reliable.

Why
- Prioritizes extraction work on sections most likely to contain meaningful strings (reduces noise, improves accuracy, and speeds downstream processing).
- Expands import detection so symbol-based tagging and metadata are more complete and dependable for analysis and scoring.

What it does
- Introduces a weight field on section metadata and computes heuristic weights for ELF, PE and Mach-O sections to guide string extraction priority.
- Enhances ELF symbol extraction to consider dynamic and regular symbol tables, accept global/weak bindings and multiple symbol types, skip empty names, and expose a conservative hook for future library attribution.
- Re-exports parsers to simplify access from the library surface.
- Adds unit and integration tests that validate section classification, weight calculation, and symbol filtering behavior.
- Updates public docs and examples to reflect the implemented container parsing, section weighting, and import/export capabilities.
- Normalizes GitHub Actions workflow YAML formatting and trims minor linting/format issues for readability (no functional CI behavior change).

Tests and validation
- Adds comprehensive unit tests for section weight heuristics and symbol-filtering criteria.
- Adds integration tests that compile/run small binaries (when available) to exercise import/export extraction and section-weight semantics.
- Tests ensure sections receive positive weights and that string-type sections score higher than code sections.

Notes / Future work
- Library-level mapping of symbols to specific shared libraries (via PLT/GOT/relocation analysis) remains a planned enhancement.
- String extraction, semantic classification, ranking, and advanced CLI features continue to be developed; the new weights are intended to improve those upcoming pipelines.

Documentation
- Adds a development standards document to align contributors on quality, testing, and tooling expectations.
- Updates architecture, CLI, quickstart, and README content to accurately reflect current capabilities and the new weighting / symbol extraction behavior.

No issue reference.

This PR optimizes the `JSONFileParseError::path()` method to return by const reference instead of by value, eliminating unnecessary copying of `std::filesystem::path` objects when accessing the file path from exceptions.

author: shijikori
body:
Now to form a trilogy of wifi patches...

I've reworked the reload function of the network module to include retries after figuring out by experimentation that the wait time for SDIO was greatly exaggerated. The time savings made by the reduction in waiting time allows me to reasonably implement a retry loop in the reloading of the network, increasing boot times again.

Since the loop only happens as many times as needed for a maximum number of attempts, the increase in boot times should be marginal unless the device really doesn't want to get out of bed.

Overall, this should reduce the time to boot caused by the network module. I also built infrastructure ready to use to decouple the maximum wait time and the maximum number of attempts, in the event that we may make these configurable.

# Fix map::at error when using -i flag without -e flag

## Summary
Fixes a copy-paste bug in the `parse_ignore` function that caused `jsonschema lint` to crash with "unexpected error: map::at" when users provided the `-i` (ignore) flag without also providing the `-e` (extension) flag.

**Root cause**: Line 421 in `src/utils.cc` was checking if the "i" option exists but then incorrectly accessing `options.at("e")` instead of `options.at("i")`, causing `std::map::at` to throw `std::out_of_range` when the "e" key doesn't exist.

**Fix**: Changed `options.at("e")` to `options.at("i")` to access the correct option map key.

Modifies the `jsonschema lint --fix` command to only write files when actual lint transformations are applied. Previously, files without any lint warnings would still be prettified during `--fix`, creating unnecessary formatting noise when running the linter on large codebases.

The fix adds a comparison check `if (copy != entry.second)` before writing the file, leveraging the existing `operator==` for JSON comparison to detect when transformations have actually occurred.

# Implement gunzip function for GZIP decompression

## Summary
Adds a new `gunzip(std::istream &stream)` function to the gzip module that decompresses GZIP-compressed input streams into strings. The implementation uses zlib's inflate functions (inflateInit2, inflate, inflateEnd) and follows the same error handling patterns as the existing `gzip` function. Includes comprehensive tests covering round-trip compression/decompression, empty strings, longer content, and error handling for invalid data.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify zlib parameters are correct** - Confirm `16 + MAX_WBITS` parameter in `inflateInit2` is correct for gzip format decompression (this is critical for compatibility)
- [ ] **Test memory efficiency with large files** - The implementation reads entire stream into memory first, which could be problematic for very large compressed files
- [ ] **Validate error handling completeness** - Verify all zlib error codes are properly handled, especially edge cases like truncated or corrupted gzip data
- [ ] **Test round-trip compatibility** - Verify data compressed with `gzip()` can be successfully decompressed with `gunzip()` for various data types and sizes

### Notes
The API mirrors the existing `gzip` function design but takes an `std::istream&` instead of `string_view` to match the requirement. The function signature exactly matches the specification provided in the task description.

body:
This pull request completes the implementation of the driven-adapters layer for the Loan microservice, enabling full persistence of loan requests using PostgreSQL and reactive programming via R2DBC.

**🔹 Technologies & Strategy**
- Database: PostgreSQL
- Persistence Layer: Spring Data R2DBC
- Reactive Programming: All operations are non-blocking and return Mono/Flux types.
- Mapping: Explicit separation between domain models and persistence entities using dedicated mappers.

**🔹 Entities**
- LoanEntity: Represents the persisted loan request, including identification number, amount, deadline, adjudication date, loan type ID, and status.
- LoanTypeEntity: Encapsulates loan type rules such as interest rate, minimum base salary, and maximum deadline.

**🔹 Repository Adapters**
- ReactiveRepositoryAdapter: Implements domain interfaces (LoanRepository, LoanTypeRepository) using reactive R2DBC repositories.
- Includes methods for:
- Creating loan requests.
- Updating loan status.
- Retrieving loans by identification number.
- Creating and listing loan types.

**🔹 Design Principles**
- Clean separation between domain and persistence layers.
- No exception handling within adapters to preserve purity; error management is delegated to upper layers.
- Enum mapping handled natively by R2DBC without JPA annotations like `@Enumerated.`

**🔹 Outcome**
- The microservice is now capable of persisting and retrieving loan-related data in a fully reactive, scalable, and decoupled manner.
- This layer completes the infrastructure required to support the domain use cases and prepares the system for integration with entry-points and external services.

author: parthosa
body:
Fixes #1752

## Motivation

AutoTuner currently does not recommend dynamic allocation properties on GPU runs when `spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled=true`. This may cause GPU runs to use the same values for dynamic allocation properties as CPU runs. Now, for jobs that do not have enough concurrent tasks to saturate those executors, this leads to over-provisioning and inflated executor uptime on GPU. This can lead to higher or comparable job runtime despite having better stage performance on GPU.

## What this PR does

When dynamic allocation is enabled, AutoTuner now recommends GPU-side executor counts derived from CPU logs using a cores-ratio formula. This ensures that unnecessary executors are not allocated. Additionally, it aligns `spark.executor.instances` with the tuned initial executors to avoid contradictory recommendations.

## Tuning Rule (applied when `spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled=true`)

For each of the following properties, the GPU recommendation is computed from the CPU value using the cores ratio and floored to an integer with minimum 1:

- `spark.dynamicAllocation.initialExecutors`
- `spark.dynamicAllocation.minExecutors`
- `spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors`

Formula:

```
GPU_value = max(1, floor(CPU_value × CPU_cores / GPU_cores))
```

Additionally, `spark.executor.instances` is set to match the tuned `spark.dynamicAllocation.initialExecutors` (taking into account any higher already-recommended instance count).

If dynamic allocation is disabled, any existing recommendations for these three dynamic-allocation properties are removed.

## Key Changes

- `core/src/main/resources/bootstrap/tuningTable.yaml`
  - Added tuning entries for `spark.dynamicAllocation.initialExecutors`, `spark.dynamicAllocation.minExecutors`, and `spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors`.

- `core/src/main/scala/com/nvidia/spark/rapids/tool/tuning/AutoTuner.scala`
  - New `ignoreRecommendation` helper to centralize skip/limited-logic/user-enforced checks.
  - New `removeRecommendation` helper used when dynamic allocation is disabled.
  - New `recommendDynamicAllocationConfigs(gpuExecCores: Int)` implementing the cores-ratio formula and coordinating `spark.executor.instances` with `initialExecutors`.
  - Invoked dynamic-allocation recommendation during cluster-level recommendation flow.
  - Added user-facing comment generator `commentForDynamicAllocationAdjustment(...)` to explain adjustments.

- `core/src/main/scala/com/nvidia/spark/rapids/tool/tuning/TuningEntryTrait.scala`
  - Made `tunedValue` getter public to allow cross-entry coordination (e.g., computing max across recommended values).

- Tests: `core/src/test/scala/com/nvidia/spark/rapids/tool/tuning/QualificationAutoTunerSuite.scala`
  - Added coverage for:
    - Dynamic allocation enabled: verifies tuned `initial/min/maxExecutors` and aligned `executor.instances` with explanatory comments.
    - Dynamic allocation disabled: verifies no dynamic-allocation recommendations are emitted.
    - Multiple CPU↔GPU core ratios (increase, decrease, no change) using `DynamicAllocationInfo` cases.
    - Edge cases (zero/negative CPU values) to ensure proper min bound handling.
    - Honoring target-cluster overrides: respects enforced `initialExecutors`/`minExecutors` and preserves source `maxExecutors`; emits enforcement/preservation comments.
    - Bumping `spark.executor.instances` up when an enforced `minExecutors` requires a higher starting value.

## Example

CPU: 8 cores/executor, GPU: 16 cores/executor, CPU values initial=12, min=12, max=30

Recommended:

- `spark.dynamicAllocation.initialExecutors=6`
- `spark.dynamicAllocation.minExecutors=6`
- `spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors=15`
- `spark.executor.instances=6` (aligned with initialExecutors)

## Notes for reviewers
- Core logic is in the function `recommendDynamicAllocationConfigs()`
- Coordination between `spark.dynamicAllocation.initialExecutors` and `spark.executor.instances` and the handling of user-enforced values is critical.

## Summary

Adds a Doctrine-driven **Indoctrination Engine** for onboarding, training, and certifying agents before they're permitted to operate under the Bridge. This is the gatekeeper: **no agent gets deployed without indoctrination**.

## Features

### 🔧 Backend Engine

New `bridge_backend/bridge_core/engines/indoctrination/` module with complete agent lifecycle management:

- **Onboarding** → Register new agents with metadata (name, role, specialties)
- **Doctrine Alignment** → Load doctrine scrolls & required policies for the agent's domain
- **Certification** → Run capability checks and issue Vault-logged certificates with unique seals
- **Revocation** → De-certify or retire an agent if doctrine shifts

### 📡 API Endpoints

```
POST   /engines/indoctrination/onboard        # Register new agent
POST   /engines/indoctrination/{aid}/certify  # Issue certification
POST   /engines/indoctrination/{aid}/revoke   # Revoke agent access
GET    /engines/indoctrination/agents         # List all agents
```

### 📜 Doctrine Scrolls

New `DOCTRINE/indoctrination/` folder containing:

**lore.md** - Indoctrination Doctrine v1:
```markdown
- Every agent must align with Sovereign Doctrine before deployment.
- Certificates are seals of trust: append-only, never backdated.
- Revocation is not punishment — it is containment of drift.
```

**policy.yaml** - Certification constraints:
```yaml
version: v1
constraints:
  certification_required: true
checks:
  - id: doctrine_alignment
    description: "Verify agent training against doctrine scrolls"
```

### 🎨 Frontend Panel

New **IndoctrinationPanel** component accessible at `/indoctrination`:

- Simple form to onboard agents (name, role, comma-separated specialties)
- Live agent list with real-time status updates
- Visual certification indicators: ✅ certified | ⏳ onboarded

### 🧪 Tests

Comprehensive test coverage in `bridge_backend/tests/test_indoctrination_engine.py`:
- Onboard and certify workflow validation
- Revocation workflow testing
- All tests passing ✅

## Screenshots

**Empty Indoctrination Panel:**

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc155dd9-e30c-49de-b24a-8c578433dd7d)

**Working Panel with Onboarded Agents:**

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6a3197b-5cbd-4fdf-838b-ec7e5506c5a3)

## Why This Matters

The Bridge can now indoctrinate agents before deployment:

✅ **Preventing rogue or misaligned behavior** - All agents must pass through indoctrination  
✅ **Certifying compliance with Sovereign Doctrine** - Doctrine alignment verified and sealed  
✅ **Auditing all onboarding and revocations in Vault** - Complete audit trail in `vault/indoctrination/`

## Technical Details

- **Clean integration**: Follows existing engine patterns (autonomy, parser, truth)
- **Minimal changes**: 197 lines added across 9 files
- **Vault persistence**: All agent records stored as JSON with unique IDs
- **No breaking changes**: All existing tests continue to pass
- **Production ready**: Vault directory excluded via .gitignore

__init__.py

from .service import IndoctrinationEngine
__all__ = ["IndoctrinationEngine"]

service.py

from pathlib import Path
import json, uuid
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Dict, Any, List

VAULT = Path("vault") / "indoctrination"
VAULT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def now_iso():
    return datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + "Z"

class IndoctrinationEngine:
    def __init__(self):
        self.registry: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}

    def onboard(self, name: str, role: str, specialties: List[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        aid = str(uuid.uuid4())
        rec = {
            "id": aid,
            "name": name,
            "role": role,
            "specialties": specialties,
            "status": "onboarded",
            "created_at": now_iso(),
            "certified": False,
            "certificates": [],
        }
        self.registry[aid] = rec
        self._write_vault(aid, rec)
        return rec

    def certify(self, aid: str, doctrine: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        agent = self.registry.get(aid)
        if not agent:
            raise ValueError("Agent not found")
        cert = {
            "doctrine": doctrine,
            "ts": now_iso(),
            "seal": str(uuid.uuid4()),
        }
        agent["certified"] = True
        agent["status"] = "certified"
        agent["certificates"].append(cert)
        self._write_vault(aid, agent)
        return cert

    def revoke(self, aid: str, reason: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        agent = self.registry.get(aid)
        if not agent:
            raise ValueError("Agent not found")
        agent["status"] = "revoked"
        agent["revoked_reason"] = reason
        agent["revoked_at"] = now_iso()
        self._write_vault(aid, agent)
        return agent

    def list_agents(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        return list(self.registry.values())

    def _write_vault(self, aid: str, rec: Dict[str, Any]):
        out = VAULT / f"{aid}.json"
        out.write_text(json.dumps(rec, indent=2))

routes.py

from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import List
from .service import IndoctrinationEngine

router = APIRouter(prefix="/engines/indoctrination", tags=["indoctrination"])
E = IndoctrinationEngine()

class OnboardIn(BaseModel):
    name: str
    role: str
    specialties: List[str]

class CertifyIn(BaseModel):
    doctrine: str

class RevokeIn(BaseModel):
    reason: str

@router.post("/onboard")
def onboard(data: OnboardIn):
    return E.onboard(data.name, data.role, data.specialties)

@router.post("/{aid}/certify")
def certify(aid: str, data: CertifyIn):
    try:
        return E.certify(aid, data.doctrine)
    except Exception as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=str(e))

@router.post("/{aid}/revoke")
def revoke(aid: str, data: RevokeIn):
    try:
        return E.revoke(aid, data.reason)
    except Exception as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=str(e))

@router.get("/agents")
def list_agents():
    return E.list_agents()

author: therealmichaelwang
body:
Added a Einsum IR that is more flexible than the previous. The Einsum IR's grammar can be described as the following:

## Einsum IR Grammar

### Base Node Type
- **PointwiseNode**: Abstract base class for all AST nodes in the Einsum Pointwise Expression IR

### Pointwise Expression Nodes

- **PointwiseNamedField**
  - Represents a named field/variable (e.g., tensor alias or index variable)
  - Contains: `name: str`

- **PointwiseAccess**
  - Represents tensor access like `a[i, j]`
  - Contains: `alias: PointwiseNode`, `idxs: tuple[PointwiseNode, ...]`

- **PointwiseLiteral**
  - Represents a scalar literal/constant value
  - Contains: `val: float`

- **PointwiseOp**
  - Represents operations on pointwise expressions (e.g., +, *, -, /)
  - Contains: `op: Callable`, `args: tuple[PointwiseNode, ...]`
  - Note: Non-commutative operations must be binary (max 2 args)

### Sparse Tensor Operations

- **GetSparseCoordArray**
  - Gets the coordinate array of a sparse tensor in COO format
  - Contains: `sparse_tensor: PointwiseNode`

- **GetSparseValueArray**
  - Gets the value array of a sparse tensor in COO format
  - Contains: `sparse_tensor: PointwiseNode`

### Einsum Operations

- **Einsum**
  - Represents an einsum operation that maps and aggregates pointwise expressions
  - Contains:
    - `reduceOp: Callable` - The reduction operation (e.g., +=, max=, min=)
    - `output: PointwiseNode` - The output tensor
    - `output_fields: tuple[PointwiseNode, ...]` - Output indices (e.g., i, j)
    - `pointwise_expr: PointwiseNode` - The expression to map and reduce

### Top-Level Structure

- **EinsumPlan**
  - A plan containing multiple einsum operations
  - Contains:
    - `bodies: tuple[Einsum, ...]` - List of einsum operations
    - `returnValues: tuple[PointwiseNode, ...]` - Values to return

### Key Properties
- All nodes inherit from `PointwiseNode` and implement the `Term` interface
- Nodes support tree traversal through `children` properties
- The IR supports both dense and sparse tensor operations
- Reduction operations include: `overwrite (=)`, `add (+=)`, `sub (-=)`, `mul (*=)`, `max (max=)`, `min (min=)`, etc.

author: alpakash
body:
This PR introduces significant enhancements to the Pomodoro clock functionality, adding configurable audio feedback, improved UI/UX, and better window management. The changes focus on creating a more polished and user-friendly time tracking experience. 

1. Notes
- Basically I wanted an integrated pomodoro which queus me with sound every 10th minute (so I can write my findings of my current pomodoro task inside Obsidian).
- I also improved the ClockApp electron window since the old version was too small and clunky.
- I've tested the new features locally on my Macbook M2.

🔄 Minimal Touch Points with other application parts

  1. New API Endpoint: Added showClock to window router - purely additive
  2. New Atoms: Added 5 sound preference atoms - isolated storage, no conflicts
  3. Enhanced Clock IPC: Added new channels without modifying existing ones
  4. Audio Hook: Self-contained, only affects focus sessions

  🎵 New Features

1. Audio Feedback System

  - Configurable Sound Cues: Added comprehensive audio system with 5 configurable sound options:
    - Focus session start sounds
    - Interval milestone notifications (every 10 minutes)
    - Focus session completion sounds
    - Break session start sounds
    - Break session completion sounds
  - Smart Audio Management: Sounds are session-aware to prevent duplicates and use Web Audio API for consistent playback
  - User Controls: Individual toggles for each sound type in the focus settings

2. Enhanced Clock Window

  - Responsive Design: Clock window now supports two modes:
    - Detailed view (340x230px): Full information display
    - Minimal view (200x109px): Compact time-only display
  - Persistent Window State: Remembers window position, size mode, and pin status between sessions
  - Improved Styling: Beautiful new CSS with better typography, colors, and visual hierarchy
  - Pin/Unpin Functionality: Toggle always-on-top behavior with visual feedback

  🔧 Technical Improvements

  Window Management

  - Smart Positioning: Clock window remembers its last position and size
  - Bounds Management: Automatic saving of window state with debounced file operations
  - IPC Enhancement: New channels for window state management and size mode switching

  Code Quality

  - Type Safety: Enhanced TypeScript definitions for clock window state management
  - Performance: Optimized re-rendering and state updates
  - Error Handling: Better error boundaries and user feedback

  UI/UX Enhancements

  - Sidebar Polish: Fixed padding issues for better visual consistency
  - Clock Integration: Added show clock functionality from main application
  - Responsive Behavior: Clock adapts gracefully to different content sizes

  📁 Files Modified

  - src/main/windows/clock.ts - Core window management and state persistence
  - src/renderer/clock/ClockApp.tsx - Enhanced UI with dual view modes
  - src/renderer/clock/clock.css - Complete visual redesign
  - src/hooks/usePomodoroSounds.ts - New audio feedback system
  - src/pages/focus/index.tsx & src/pages/focus/components/ActiveSession.tsx - Sound integration
  - src/context/board.ts & src/context/localKey.ts - Sound preference storage
  - Multiple IPC and API files for enhanced communication

  🧪 Testing Notes

  - Clock window state persistence across app restarts
  - Audio cues trigger correctly at session boundaries and intervals
  - Window resizing and repositioning works smoothly
  - Pin/unpin functionality maintains proper z-index behavior

  📱 User Experience

  - More intuitive clock interface with clear visual hierarchy
  - Customizable audio feedback enhances focus session awareness
  - Persistent window preferences reduce setup friction
  - Cleaner, more professional appearance

⚙️  Latest Update: Cross-Platform Compatibility
  - Visual Effects: macOS-specific vibrancy and visualEffectState now only apply on macOS, preventing errors on Windows/Linux
  - Always-On-Top: Added platform-specific handling with error recovery - macOS uses "screen-saver" level, other platforms use standard behavior
  - Error Handling: Graceful degradation when platform-specific features fail, with proper logging

  Why This Matters: Ensures the clock window works reliably across all supported platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux) without breaking functionality or throwing errors on non-macOS systems.

  ---
  Breaking Changes: None - all new features are opt-in with sensible defaults.

author: tiegz
body:
When parsing a Maven pom.xml and lockfile pair, the lockfile will hold the source of truth for `<scope>`. The manifest may not have that value, and the parent pom may not be available to resolve `<scope>`. Bibliothecary should just return `nil` instead of defaulting to "runtime" and let the client use the lockfile to find the actual value to avoid erroneous `<scope>` assumptions.

(also, a few Rubocop lints)

author: alexflorisca
body:
## Overview

This PR implements a comprehensive StrategyManager system that provides versioning, performance tracking, lineage management, and safe promotion/rollback capabilities for trading strategies.

## Key Components Implemented

### 1. StrategyRegistry (Task 8.1) ✅
- Complete strategy registration with version management
- Comprehensive metadata tracking (creation date, author, description, tags, status)
- Strategy serialization/deserialization for persistence
- Integrity validation and consistency checking
- Automatic version numbering with change tracking

### 2. PerformanceTracker (Task 8.2) ✅
- Real-time strategy performance metrics tracking
- Comprehensive performance calculations (Sharpe ratio, drawdown, win rate, etc.)
- Trade history storage and retrieval with filtering
- Performance comparison utilities between strategies
- Regime-specific performance analysis
- Efficient caching system for performance metrics

### 3. StrategyLineageTracker (Task 8.3) ✅
- Parent-child relationship tracking for strategy evolution
- Branching capabilities for parallel strategy development
- Strategy merging with conflict resolution
- Detailed change tracking with impact analysis
- Evolution visualization (Mermaid and DOT diagrams)
- Change propagation analysis across strategy lineage

### 4. StrategyManager (Task 8.4) ✅
- Orchestrates all components with promotion/rollback capabilities
- Configurable validation gates (performance, trades, drawdown, Sharpe ratio, win rate)
- Safe strategy promotion pipeline: experimental → testing → production
- Automatic rollback triggers for performance degradation
- Manual override capabilities for emergency situations
- Comprehensive strategy status reporting

## Key Features

- **Safety First**: Multiple validation gates prevent poor strategies from reaching production
- **Automatic Monitoring**: Real-time performance monitoring with automatic rollback triggers
- **Comprehensive Tracking**: Full lineage, performance, and change history
- **Flexible Configuration**: Configurable thresholds for validation and rollback
- **Database Integration**: Full database model support for persistence
- **Extensive Testing**: 75+ comprehensive tests covering all functionality

## Database Changes

- Added StrategyRegistry, StrategyVersion, StrategyPerformance tables
- Added StrategyLineage table for evolutionary tracking
- Enhanced existing models with strategy management support

## Testing

- **25 tests** for StrategyManager functionality
- **28 tests** for StrategyLineageTracker
- **22 tests** for PerformanceTracker  
- **25 tests** for StrategyRegistry
- **100% test coverage** for all new components

## Requirements Addressed

- ✅ 4.3: Strategy performance tracking and comparison
- ✅ 4.4: Strategy promotion and rollback capabilities  
- ✅ 5.1: Strategy registry with version control
- ✅ 5.2: Strategy lineage tracking for evolutionary development
- ✅ 5.3: Strategy metadata tracking and validation
- ✅ 7.1: Validation gates for strategy promotion
- ✅ 7.2: Automatic rollback capabilities

## Breaking Changes

None - this is a new system that extends existing functionality.

## Migration Notes

No migration required - all new tables and functionality.

body: ## What does this change? Updates the secure-anonymous-submission link on Callout components (like the one on this page: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2025/oct/01/airline-industry-workers-share-your-experiences#6311788 - components which are currently used solely by the Community Team): * From: **SecureDrop** https://www.theguardian.com/securedrop * To: **Secure Messaging** https://www.theguardian.com/tips - detailing Secure Messaging/Coverdrop, as well as other communication options including SecureDrop (page initially setup in [January 2025](https://github.com/guardian/interactives/issues/2202)) (note from @hoyla : _In running text we use the convention "Secure Messaging" even though the logo itself is "SecureMessaging"._) ## Why? I noticed today that callouts on www.theguardian.com still point to SecureDrop - Secure Messaging represents a generally more user-friendly way to submit tips securely & anonymously than the steps required for submitting to SecureDrop, so ideally, if readers _want_ to use high-security routes like this, we should offer them Secure Messaging for preference. Note that the new link is to a page that still lists SecureDrop as an _option_, as it is better for, eg, submitting files, photos, etc. As these Callout components are used by the Community Team, we'll need to check they're ok with the change, and ensure they have access to read Secure Messaging messages intended for them. ## Screenshots | Before | After | | ----------- | ---------- | | | | ## Related For subsequent/separate PRs: * SecureDrop is also in [many footer definitions](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aguardian%2Fdotcom-rendering+%22https%3A%2F%2Fwww.theguardian.com%2Fsecuredrop%22&type=code) in this project (a refactor might be a good idea to reduce duplication?) * From @hoyla about SecureDrop footers/headers: _"Part of the convention for all SecureDrop sites is to include that info in such places"_ - so we should retain them. * This wording is also in a mobile-apps-api template: https://github.com/guardian/mobile-apps-api/blob/3d9f47cb7bd6e0a7c9e7e1deb64bbd07121d4198/common-play/src/main/scala/views/campaigns/callouts/calloutForm.scala.html#L97

body:
This pull request introduces multiple improvements and new features across the GroceryApp solution, focusing on user role support, enhanced UI for product and grocery list management, and improved test and development workflows. The most significant changes include the introduction of user roles (such as Admin), updates to the UI for better data display and user interaction, and the addition of a GitHub Actions workflow for automated MAUI unit testing.

**Authentication and Authorization Enhancements:**

* Added a `Role` enum to `Grocery.Core.Enums` and extended the `Client` model to support user roles, with constructors and default values. The `ClientRepository` now assigns the `Admin` role to a specific user. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0745c54bd2236fa55f5647a66f609699272ea678290467b345a1f78ab3d28b18R1-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-07aaf804dd7ec9ca6c11436b3484fac046b8997c8c9c526c5a0c0059d2d64715R2-R19) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-2627d2bc1d0b49377855892109e3135b9d24f10d3e829a2643ee60bfc8475a68L16-R16)
* Updated `GroceryListViewModel` to include the current client and expose a command to show bought products, only available to Admin users. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f03a099ad40be8f04842f8ccc05fed12643b0cb4ee178c04b19132d42c85b223R13-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f03a099ad40be8f04842f8ccc05fed12643b0cb4ee178c04b19132d42c85b223R44-R53)

**UI and User Experience Improvements:**

* Enhanced several XAML views (`BestSellingProductsView`, `BoughtProductsView`, `GroceryListItemsView`, `GroceryListsView`) to display more detailed information, improve layout, and better handle empty states. This includes table headers, product rankings, client and grocery list names, and interactive buttons for modifying item amounts. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-495031e342cca7f7e1dc53ecb436fd68d811263b412f60f0fd29448966798fd1R29-R33) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-495031e342cca7f7e1dc53ecb436fd68d811263b412f60f0fd29448966798fd1R46-R59) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-873738d887b66c76e14e1752865b5a32bf508caf2b336bfd9c81bb596da81866R20-R25) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-873738d887b66c76e14e1752865b5a32bf508caf2b336bfd9c81bb596da81866L37-R46) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-61d5d43038bf4b4a77d20fc3f19df6615feb091c7bc43fac83a617793dc349b4L27-R77) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-3dc2ede781fcf6a8be0ac2811b1e55766efdaed2b8fc4c05a4d7ade147129740L11-R17) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-3dc2ede781fcf6a8be0ac2811b1e55766efdaed2b8fc4c05a4d7ade147129740R41)

**Business Logic and Data Handling:**

* Implemented the `BoughtProductsService.Get` method to retrieve bought products for a selected product, joining data from clients, grocery lists, and products.
* Improved `GroceryListItemsService.GetBestSellingProducts` to calculate and return the top-selling products, including error handling.
* Updated `BoughtProductsViewModel` to refresh the bought products list when a new product is selected.

**Development Workflow and Testing:**

* Added a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/maui-tests.yml`) for running MAUI unit tests on push and pull requests to main and development branches.
* Updated the project file to only target `net8.0-android` by default, likely to streamline builds and tests.

**Documentation:**

* Added a section to `README.md` describing the Git Flow branching strategy used in the project.

	Please provide enough information so that others can review your PR.
	Once created, your PR will be automatically labeled according to changed files.
	Learn more about contributing: https://github.com/biomejs/biome/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Summary

The works of this PR are two:
- refactors parse and analyzer diagnostics to be able to accept an offset so they can be emitted properly inside language snippets
- refactors the implementation of the embedded languages to make them more generic and workspace aware


### Parse and Analyzer diagnostics

Both `ParseDiagnostic` and `AnalyzerDiagnostic` now have an `advice_offset` and a `set_location_offset` method that is in charge of changing the `TextRange` of the `Location` and the code frame of the advices.

In order to implement this new feature, I implemented the following refactors:
- The `Diagnostic` trait is now implemented via `impl` and not via derive. That was required because `location` must be created dynamically. Plus, `#[advice]` can't be used anymore due to the following 
- The `Advise` trait must be implemented at the Diagnostic level, so we can read `advice_offset` and use it in case it is set when printing the code frames.

### Workspace snippets

Embedded nodes/snippets were parsed inside the `open_file_internal` using a custom logic (we checked if the file is `HTML`). We don't do this anymore. We check if `DocumentFileSource::can_contain_embeds`, and if `true`, we eventually call **a new parse capability added in this PR**. This parsing capability is implemented at the language level.

This new architecture will allow us to parse other language snippets while keeping the Workspace implementation generic. For example, we will be able to parse snippets in JavaScript, such as CSS-in-JS, GraphQL queries, etc.

### More refactors
- `AnyParse` is now an enum for the former `AnyParse`, now called `NodeParse` and a new variant `EmbeddedNode`. This enum exposes `unwrap_*` methods to "safely" pull root nodes or root embedded nodes while making methods inside the Workspace generic.
- `into_diagnostics` has been renamed to `into_serde_diagnostics`
- `EmbeddedSnippets` is now an `enum` with language variants. This is now generic, and not HTML-centric
- Enabled linting inside the `html` configuration, so diagnostics can be pulled
- `JsParseOption` are now `Copy`, which is in line with the other `*ParseOption` of the other languages

<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve?-->

<!-- Link any relevant issues if necessary or include a transcript of any Discord discussion. -->

<!-- If you create a user-facing change, please write a changeset: https://github.com/biomejs/biome/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#writing-a-changeset (your changeset is often a good starting point for this summary as well) -->

Making everything generic, as well as the pull of diagnostics, will allow us to implement the `fix_file` for embedded nodes too. I will do this in another PR, because it will require further changes, which I didn't want to add.

## Test Plan

author: jhernand
body:
Currently the storage layer uses the empty tenancy logic by default. This is to avoid setting it explicily in unit tests that aren't about tenancy. A potential side effect of that is that if some code path forgets to explicitly set it can result in a security vulnerability. To avoid that this patch changes the storage layer so that the the tenancy logic is required, and is explicitly set in all the places where it is needed.

Note that this doesn't change the behaviour of the system, as the tenancy logic was already explicitly set when the server was started.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

This PR converts the Ultra-Light-Fast-Generic-Face-Detector from face detection to general COCO object detection, and changes the input size from 4:3 aspect ratio to 640x640 square format.

## Changes Summary

### 1. Input Size Configuration (640x640 Square)

Modified the configuration files to support square 640x640 input instead of the original 4:3 aspect ratio (e.g., 320x240, 640x480):

- `vision/ssd/config/fd_config.py`: Updated image size to `[640, 640]` and feature maps to `[[80, 40, 20, 10], [80, 40, 20, 10]]`
- `paddle/vision/ssd/config/fd_config.py`: Applied same changes for PaddlePaddle version

This generates 23,500 anchor priors optimized for square input.

### 2. COCO Object Detection Support

Expanded the model from 2-class face detection to 81-class COCO object detection (BACKGROUND + 80 COCO categories including person, vehicles, animals, household items, etc.):

**New Files:**
- `models/coco-model-labels.txt`: All 81 class labels
- `vision/datasets/coco_dataset.py`: Complete COCO dataset loader with pycocotools integration

**Updated Files:**
- `train.py`: Added `--dataset_type coco` support alongside existing VOC format

### 3. Inference Scripts Update

Updated all detection scripts to use COCO labels and 640x640 input:

- `convert_to_onnx.py`: Export models with 640x640 input and 81 classes
- `detect_imgs.py`: Image detection with COCO class names displayed
- `detect_imgs_onnx.py`: ONNX version for image detection
- `run_video_face_detect.py`: Video detection showing object categories
- `run_video_face_detect_onnx.py`: ONNX video detection

All scripts now display class names and confidence scores on detected objects.

### 4. Documentation & Testing

**New Documentation:**
- `COCO_USAGE.md`: Complete English guide covering training, inference, dataset structure, and troubleshooting
- `CHANGES_SUMMARY_CN.md`: Chinese summary of all changes (中文版本修改摘要)
- `test_coco_config.py`: Quick verification script to validate the setup

## Technical Details

### Network Architecture
Both RFB and Slim networks now support 81 classes:
- Input: `[1, 3, 640, 640]`
- Scores output: `[1, 23500, 81]`
- Boxes output: `[1, 23500, 4]`

### COCO Dataset Structure
The COCO dataset loader expects standard format:
```
/path/to/coco/
├── train2017/
├── val2017/
└── annotations/
    ├── instances_train2017.json
    └── instances_val2017.json
```

### Usage Example

**Training:**
```bash
python train.py \
    --dataset_type coco \
    --datasets /path/to/coco/train2017 \
    --validation_dataset /path/to/coco/val2017 \
    --input_size 640 \
    --net RFB \
    --batch_size 16
```

**Inference:**
```bash
python detect_imgs.py \
    --net_type RFB \
    --input_size 640 \
    --path ./images \
    --threshold 0.5
```

## Important Notes

1. **Model Retraining Required**: Pretrained face detection weights are incompatible with 81 classes. You must retrain on COCO dataset.

2. **Memory Requirements**: 640x640 input requires more GPU memory than 320x240. Recommended batch size: 8-16.

3. **Backward Compatibility**: Original face detection functionality is preserved. Use `--dataset_type voc` for face detection tasks.

4. **Verification**: Run `python test_coco_config.py` to verify the setup.

## Testing

All changes have been verified:
- ✅ Configuration loads correctly (640x640, 81 classes, 23,500 priors)
- ✅ Both RFB and Slim networks functional with 81 classes
- ✅ Forward pass works correctly
- ✅ COCO dataset loader tested
- ✅ All imports successful

## Files Changed

**Modified (8 files):** Configuration files, training script, inference scripts  
**Added (5 files):** COCO dataset loader, labels file, documentation, test script  
**Statistics:** +644 lines, -66 lines

## Fix: Handle global field arrays and field objects in image_hot_spots tag

### Problem
When using global field references like `maps:visitor_trail_hot_spots`, the tag fails with:
- `Call to a member function value() on array` 
- `array_key_exists(): Argument #1 ($key) must be a valid array offset type`

### Solution
Modified `HotSpotImageTag.php` to handle both:
- **Field objects** (page-level fields): Calls `->value()` method as before
- **Direct data arrays** (global field references): Uses the data directly

### Usage Examples
```antlers
<!-- Page-level field (existing functionality) -->
{{ image_hot_spots field="image_hot_spots_field" }}

<!-- Global field reference (new functionality) -->
{{ image_hot_spots field="maps:visitor_trail_hot_spots" }}
```

### Backward Compatibility
✅ Fully backward compatible - no breaking changes
✅ Existing implementations continue to work unchanged

author: manciniedoardo
body:
Thank you for your Pull Request! We have developed this task checklist from the [Development Process Guide](https://pharmaverse.github.io/admiral/CONTRIBUTING.html#detailed-development-process) to help with the final steps of the process. Completing the below tasks helps to ensure our reviewers can maximize their time on your code as well as making sure the admiral family codebase remains robust and consistent.   

Please check off each taskbox as an acknowledgment that you completed the task or check off that it is not relevant to your Pull Request. This checklist is part of the Github Action workflows and the Pull Request will not be merged into the `main` branch until you have checked off each task.

- [ ] Place Closes #<insert_issue_number> into the beginning of your Pull Request Title (Use Edit button in top-right if you need to update)
- [ ] Code is formatted according to the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/). Run `styler::style_file()` to style R and Rmd files
- [ ] Updated relevant unit tests or have written new unit tests, which should consider realistic data scenarios and edge cases, e.g. empty datasets, errors, boundary cases etc. - See [Unit Test Guide](https://pharmaverse.github.io/admiraldev/articles/unit_test_guidance.html#tests-should-be-robust-to-cover-realistic-data-scenarios)
- [ ] If you removed/replaced any function and/or function parameters, did you fully follow the [deprecation guidance](https://pharmaverse.github.io/admiraldev/articles/programming_strategy.html#deprecation)?
- [ ] Update to all relevant roxygen headers and examples, including keywords and families. Refer to the [categorization of functions](https://pharmaverse.github.io/admiraldev/articles/programming_strategy.html#categorization-of-functions) to tag appropriate keyword/family.
- [ ] Run `devtools::document()` so all `.Rd` files in the `man` folder and the `NAMESPACE` file in the project root are updated appropriately
- [ ] Address any updates needed for vignettes and/or templates
- [ ] Update `NEWS.md` under the header `# admiral<ext> (development version)` if the changes pertain to a user-facing function (i.e. it has an `@export` tag) or documentation aimed at users (rather than developers)
- [ ] Build site `pkgdown::build_site()` and check that all affected examples are displayed correctly and that all new functions occur on the Reference page. 
- [ ] Address or fix all lintr warnings and errors - `lintr::lint_package()`
- [ ] Run `R CMD check` locally and address all errors and warnings - `devtools::check()`
- [ ] Link the issue in the Development Section on the right hand side.
- [ ] Address all merge conflicts and resolve appropriately
- [ ] Pat yourself on the back for a job well done! Much love to your accomplishment!

author: lukeafullard
body:
This commit addresses three critical bugs that could lead to incorrect scientific conclusions or crashes.

- **Bootstrap Failure Handling in fitter.py**: The bootstrap functions in `fitter.py` no longer fail silently with NaN CIs when the success rate is low. A `ValueError` is now raised if the bootstrap success rate is below 50%, ensuring that users are alerted to unreliable results.

- **Changepoint Detection with Small Datasets in changepoint_detector.py**: The `detect_changepoint_pelt` function now raises a `ValueError` when the dataset is too small for the specified `min_size`, preventing the analysis from silently falling back to a standard model.

- **Error Propagation in preprocessor.py**: The `log_transform` function now correctly handles non-positive values by setting the corresponding errors to NaN, preventing division-by-zero errors and downstream crashes.

body:
# Text-to-Image Evaluation

## Description
This PR implements the **DSG (Davidsonian Scene Graph)** metric for Pruna's evaluation system.  
DSG is an automatic evaluation framework for text-to-image models inspired by formal semantics to assess **faithfulness**.  

The metric works by:
- Generating atomic semantic tuples, dependency graphs, and questions from text prompts.  
- Evaluating generated images based on VQA consistency with dependency constraints.  

## Related Issue
Fixes #371 

## Type of Change
<!-- Mark the appropriate option with an "x" (no spaces around the "x") -->
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update

## How Has This Been Tested?
- Implemented comprehensive unit tests with mocked DSG dependencies to avoid API key requirements  
- Tested metric registration and initialization with various parameters  
- Verified the complete DSG evaluation pipeline (question generation, dependency constraints, VQA evaluation)  
- Tested error handling for missing dependencies and failed API calls  
- Validated metric integration with Pruna's evaluation system using mock data  
- Tested batch processing and state accumulation across multiple prompt-image pairs  
- Verified lazy model initialization to avoid import errors when DSG is not installed  

## Checklist
<!-- Mark items with "x" (no spaces around the "x") -->
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project  
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code  
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas  
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation  
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works  
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes  

## Additional Notes
**Key Features Implemented:**  
- `DSGMetric` class: Inherits from `StatefulMetric` with proper state management  
- **Registry integration**: Registered as `"dsg"` in `MetricRegistry` for easy access  
- **Configurable models**: Supports GPT-3.5/4 for LLM and mPLUG/InstructBLIP for VQA  
- **Dependency constraints**: Implements DSG's dependency graph logic for question scoring  
- **Error handling**: Graceful degradation when dependencies are missing or API calls fail  
- **Lazy initialization**: Models are only loaded when needed to avoid import errors  
- **Comprehensive logging**: Uses Pruna's logging system for debugging and monitoring  

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Adds a new DSG metric for text-to-image faithfulness with registry integration, lazy model loading, and comprehensive tests.
> 
> - **Metrics**:
>   - **`DSGMetric` (`src/pruna/evaluation/metrics/metric_dsg.py`)**: Implements Davidsonian Scene Graph evaluation for text-to-image (LLM question generation + VQA + dependency constraints), with lazy init of OpenAI LLM and VQA backends (`mplug-large`/`instructblip`), stateful scoring, and error handling.
>   - **Registry/Exports**: Registers as `"dsg"` and exposes via `pruna.evaluation.metrics` (`__init__.py`).
> - **Tests**:
>   - **Unit/Integration**: Add extensive tests for registration, initialization, DSG generation, VQA integration, dependency constraints, update/compute, error handling, and Task/EvaluationAgent integration (`test_dsg_implementation.py`, `tests/evaluation/test_dsg_integration.py`, `tests/evaluation/test_metric_dsg.py`).

body:
## Summary
Fixes the issue where "Start Next Task" displays "Working on: Unknown" for regular tasks. Workflow steps were working correctly, but regular tasks showed "Unknown" because the work session wasn't populated with task names.

## Changes
- **WorkTrackingService**: Added database lookups to fetch task/step names during session creation
  - For workflows: fetches workflow task and finds specific step by ID
  - For regular tasks: fetches task name directly
  - Passes `taskName` and `stepName` to `createUnifiedWorkSession()`
- **Tests**: Updated mock database to include `getTaskById` method and added assertions for task/step names

## Root Cause
When `startWorkSession()` created a new `UnifiedWorkSession`, it didn't populate the optional `taskName` and `stepName` fields. The UI fell back to "Unknown" when these fields were undefined.

## Test Plan
- [x] All existing tests pass (1097 passing)
- [x] Updated workTrackingService tests verify task/step names are set
- [x] TypeScript compilation passes
- [x] Lint passes (warnings only, no errors)
- [x] Manual testing: Start Next Task now shows actual task name

## Technical Details
The `UnifiedWorkSession` type has optional display fields meant to be populated from database relations. This fix eagerly loads these fields during session creation, preventing UI components from handling missing data.

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

With the [deprecation](https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/pull/8426) of _updateMode_ [Auto](https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/blob/master/vertical-pod-autoscaler/docs/quickstart.md#quick-start), we need to migrate our workloads to use it's only fallback implementation - _updateMode_ `Recreate`. This pull request instruments the extension VPA resource with _updateMode_ `Recreate`.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Part of https://github.com/gardener/gardener/issues/12903

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

VPA resources deployed as part of the extension should have their

```yaml
updateMode: Recreate
```

as part of the configuration.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The app was crashing on startup with a fatal `IllegalStateException` when `RecordingService` attempted to initialize sensors:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Method setCurrentState must be called on the main thread
    at androidx.lifecycle.LifecycleRegistry.enforceMainThreadIfNeeded(LifecycleRegistry.jvm.kt:297)
    at androidx.lifecycle.LifecycleRegistry.setCurrentState(LifecycleRegistry.jvm.kt:101)
    at mpdc4gsr.feature.network.data.ComprehensiveRecordingController$createManagedLifecycleOwner$1.<init>(ComprehensiveRecordingController.kt:804)
```

This prevented the service from starting, causing a `ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTimeException` and complete app crash.

## Root Cause

The issue occurred in `ComprehensiveRecordingController.createManagedLifecycleOwner()`:

1. `RecordingService.onCreate()` calls `recordingController.initializeSensors()` in a background coroutine on `Dispatchers.IO`
2. When no lifecycle owner is provided (service context), `initializeSensors()` calls `createManagedLifecycleOwner()`
3. This function was setting `LifecycleRegistry.currentState` directly on the background thread
4. Android's `LifecycleRegistry` enforces that all state transitions must occur on the main thread to ensure thread safety

## Solution

Modified `createManagedLifecycleOwner()` to properly handle threading:

- Changed from regular function to `suspend fun` 
- Wrapped the lifecycle owner creation in `withContext(Dispatchers.Main)` to ensure all state transitions execute on the main thread
- Updated documentation to clarify the threading requirement

```kotlin
private suspend fun createManagedLifecycleOwner(): LifecycleOwner {
    return withContext(Dispatchers.Main) {
        object : LifecycleOwner {
            private val lifecycleRegistry = LifecycleRegistry(this).apply {
                currentState = Lifecycle.State.INITIALIZED
                currentState = Lifecycle.State.CREATED
                currentState = Lifecycle.State.STARTED
                currentState = Lifecycle.State.RESUMED
            }
            override val lifecycle: Lifecycle get() = lifecycleRegistry
        }
    }
}
```

## Impact

- Fixes the crash on service startup
- Ensures proper thread safety for lifecycle operations per Android requirements
- No breaking changes since the calling code (`initializeSensors()`) was already a suspend function
- Minimal, surgical fix affecting only the problematic function

## Testing

- Verified successful compilation with `./gradlew :app:compileDebugKotlin`
- Reviewed codebase for similar threading issues with lifecycle operations

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

Created a professional, comprehensive README.md for the SpaceBio Semantic Search project with detailed documentation and visual architecture diagrams.

## What's New

### 📊 Visual Documentation (4 Mermaid Diagrams)

1. **System Architecture Diagram** - Complete overview of the data ingestion pipeline and search API architecture, showing how components interact from CSV download through FAISS indexing
2. **Data Flow Sequence Diagram** - Step-by-step visualization of both ingestion and search phases, illustrating the interaction between users, FastAPI, embeddings, and storage
3. **System Components Diagram** - Detailed breakdown of core components (text chunker, embeddings generator, FAISS index), data sources (Europe PMC, PubMed Central), and API endpoints
4. **Project Workflow Flowchart** - Developer-friendly guide showing the complete workflow from repository clone to deployment

### 📝 Comprehensive Documentation

The README now includes:

- **Project Overview** - Clear description of the semantic search engine for space biology publications
- **Installation Guide** - Prerequisites, virtual environment setup, and dependency installation
- **Data Ingestion Instructions** - How to populate the database with publications, including configuration options
- **API Documentation** - Complete endpoint documentation with request/response examples:
  - `/health` - System health check
  - `/search?q=...&k=5` - Semantic search with query parameters
  - `/pub/{pub_id}` - Retrieve specific publications
- **Example Queries** - Ready-to-use curl commands for common use cases
- **Technical Details** - Embedding model specs, vector index configuration, text processing parameters
- **Project Structure** - File organization and data directory layout
- **Dependencies** - Categorized list of core libraries and data processing tools
- **Development Guide** - Customization instructions for embedding models and chunk sizes
- **Statistics** - Current indexed data metrics (929 chunks, 768 dimensions)

## Why This Matters

The project had no README.md, making it difficult for users and contributors to:
- Understand what the project does
- Set up and run the application
- Use the API endpoints
- Understand the system architecture
- Contribute to the project

This comprehensive README with visual diagrams addresses all these needs, providing both high-level architectural views and detailed technical documentation.

## Example Visualization

The System Architecture diagram shows the complete flow:
```
CSV File → Ingest Pipeline → Europe PMC/PubMed Central → Parser → Chunker → Embedder → FAISS Index
                                                                                      ↓
User Query → FastAPI Server ← FAISS Search ← Semantic Encoding ← Publication JSONs
```

Built for NASA Space Apps Hackathon 🚀🔬

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Several mermaid diagrams throughout the repository were failing to render on GitHub with parse errors like:

```
Parse error on line 11: ... Expecting 'SQE', 'DOUBLECIRCLEEND', 'PE', '-)', 
'STADIUMEND', 'SUBROUTINEEND', 'PIPE', 'CYLINDEREND', 'DIAMOND_STOP', 
'TAGEND', 'TRAPEND', 'INVTRAPEND', 'UNICODE_TEXT', 'TEXT', 'TAGSTART', got 'PS'
```

The root cause was that 4 markdown files were using single backticks (`` ` ``) instead of triple backticks (`` ``` ``) to delimit mermaid code blocks. This prevented GitHub's mermaid renderer from correctly parsing the diagrams.

## Solution

### Mermaid Syntax Fixes

Fixed the following files by converting single backticks to triple backticks:

- `01-kernel-acquisition/how_linux_works/01-repo-layout.md` - Directory Relationships diagram
- `01-kernel-acquisition/how_linux_works/02-tracing-syscalls.md` - Syscall Flow diagram  
- `01-kernel-acquisition/how_linux_works/03-subsystems.md` - Subsystem interaction diagrams
- `01-kernel-acquisition/how_linux_works/04-hands-on-exercises.md` - Exercise Flow diagram

**Before:**
```markdown
`mermaid
graph TD
A[arch/] --> B[kernel/]
...
`
```

**After:**
```markdown
```mermaid
graph TD
A[arch/] --> B[kernel/]
...
```
```

### Table of Contents Enhancement

Enhanced the main `README.md` table of contents with a hierarchical structure:

- **Bold chapter headers** for improved visibility
- **Indented sub-bullets** linking to 30+ key subsection documents
- **Direct navigation** to specific topics like "Using Menuconfig", "Hardening Options", "Container Support", etc.

This makes it much easier for users to quickly find and navigate to specific content within each chapter.

## Validation

All 40 mermaid diagrams in the repository have been validated:
- ✅ 100% use correct triple backtick syntax
- ✅ All pass syntax validation (balanced brackets, proper diagram types, etc.)
- ✅ All should now render correctly on GitHub

## Impact

- Fixes rendering issues for all affected mermaid diagrams
- Improves documentation navigation and user experience
- Minimal, surgical changes (5 files: 46 insertions, 16 deletions)

body:
# Advanced Backup and Disaster Recovery System Implementation

## Description
This pull request implements a comprehensive **enterprise-grade backup and disaster recovery system** for the StelloPay payroll platform. The implementation provides complete data protection capabilities across three core files with automated scheduling, incremental backups, encryption, cross-region replication, and disaster recovery testing.

**Key Features Implemented:**
- **Core Backup Operations**: Full-featured backup system with multiple backup types (Full, Employer, Employee, Template, Insurance, Compliance)
- **Incremental Backups**: Differential backup system that only backs up changed data for storage efficiency  
- **Automated Scheduling**: Cron-like scheduling system with configurable frequencies (daily, weekly, monthly) and retention policies
- **Disaster Recovery**: Complete recovery system with multiple modes (Full, Partial, Emergency, Test)
- **Encryption & Security**: Optional encryption with user-provided keys and comprehensive access controls
- **Cross-Region Replication**: Multi-region backup redundancy for enhanced disaster recovery
- **Enterprise Management**: Organization-wide backup policies, compliance reporting, and monitoring dashboards

## Related Issue
Fixes #119  and Closes #119 - Implement Advanced Backup and Disaster Recovery

## Checklist
- [x] I have tested the changes locally
- [x] I have added/updated documentation as needed
- [x] I have reviewed the code and ensured it follows the project guidelines
- [x] I have added necessary tests (unit/integration)
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings/errors
- [x] I have checked for code formatting issues

## Additional Notes

### **Technical Implementation Details:**
- **33 backup-related functions** implemented across [payroll.rs](cci:7://file:///Users/saikiransurapalli/Desktop/stellopay-core/onchain/contracts/stello_pay_contract/src/payroll.rs:0:0-0:0)
- **Complete enterprise backup management** system in [enterprise.rs](cci:7://file:///Users/saikiransurapalli/Desktop/stellopay-core/onchain/contracts/stello_pay_contract/src/enterprise.rs:0:0-0:0) 
- **Full backup data structures** and storage helpers in [storage.rs](cci:7://file:///Users/saikiransurapalli/Desktop/stellopay-core/onchain/contracts/stello_pay_contract/src/storage.rs:0:0-0:0)
- **Multi-tenant architecture** supporting separate backup management per employer
- **Event-driven design** with comprehensive event emission for monitoring

### **Security Considerations:**
- **Multi-level authorization** (Owner, Employer, Role-based permissions)
- **Encryption at rest** with user-provided encryption keys
- **Data integrity verification** using cryptographic hashing
- **Complete audit trails** for compliance and troubleshooting

### **Performance Optimizations:**
- **Incremental backup system** reduces storage requirements
- **Efficient storage patterns** using ExtendedDataKey system
- **Batch operations** for improved performance with large datasets
- **Optimized data structures** for gas-efficient blockchain operations

### **Monitoring & Analytics:**
- **Real-time backup health dashboards**
- **Success rate tracking and trend analysis**
- **Storage utilization monitoring**
- **Compliance reporting and audit trails**

### **Deployment Impact:**
- **No breaking changes** to existing functionality
- **Backward compatible** with existing data structures
- **Zero additional dependencies** required
- **Ready for immediate production deployment**

**This implementation provides enterprise-grade reliability and security for critical payroll data protection.**

-cc @Jagadeeshftw

author: protonull
body:
This uses a number of strategies to try to weed out these weird ItemExchange bugs, whose causes remain unknown:

- Created an InventoryAccessor interface to specifically target an inventory's "contents" or "storage contents". This should avoid potential bugs coming from Minecraft attempting to equip a pickaxe as their helmet.

- Created an ItemStash record whose sole purpose is to guarantee anyone with an instance of it that you have a not-null, not-empty list of items which are themselves not-null, not-empty, and have valid amounts. All the "safely" inventory APIs have been switched over to this, meaning that it's now impossible to trade an empty-collection of items. This should avoid such potential bugs, or at least put a nice big stacktrace in the console.

- Those "safely" inventory APIs have had their inventory-cloning behaviour removed in favour of the caller doing it themselves. This should help with any potential issues caused by ClonedInventory being in control over whether a cloned-inventory can clone, etc, which may avoid situations where an inventory is cloned but not committed back when it should.

- Those "safely" inventory APIs now clone the item before passing it into Bukkit's .addItem() and .removeItem() inventory APIs. The javadoc for these functions say that the given item may be mutated by the inventory. This may have had implications where a failed transaction contaminated a subsequent successful transaction.
